column2: How much damage you deal to an enemy depends on many different variables and is calculated differently in each game mode.
When we attack an enemy in the game, a damage number will pop up on the target's head.
The color of the number represents the status of the attack. There are three colors of the damage number:
white: Generally, normal damage is displayed in white
yellow: If a critical hit is triggered, the damage text will be displayed in yellow font.
orange: there is 3 possible scenarios for orange damage numbers
Firestorm: Using wind skills to hit an enemy in a burning state will trigger the firestorm. Wind skills will increase damage by +50% in D type,
and the damage number will change to orange.  The display priority of this orange text is higher than that of critical hits, and will cover the yellow text of critical hits
Ancestral Hammer: The Barbarian's Ancestral Hammer, after using the Razor Grip (off-hand) to turn it into a giant hammer inscription,
the stunned monster will suffer 50% damage and will also be displayed in orange. This 50% damage is not mentioned in the equipment special effects and skill panel descriptions.
Big Critical Damage: Regardless of skill coefficients, various damage bonuses, or the target's immunity and vulnerability, as long as a critical hit is hit,

and the damage value of this critical hit is more than 2.2 times the damage value of the player's own (base damage) panel, it will be displayed in orange. 
Only critical hit damage will change to orange.
There are a lot of different damage types in the game:
Since there are different types of damage and possibilities to build your character there are multiple ways to optimize / increase your damage output.
All damage done takes your BASE_DMG (the number you see in your character attribute) into its calculation, so it is always good to try to improve the damage stat
1. Permanent Damage Buffs / Increased Buff Duration

These buffs are always good because they increase your damage everytime. With the right build and combination of Set-Pieces, Gems and Essences and a focus on 
 increasing your buff duration and skill cooldown through reforging and magic affixes you can have temporary buffs being always active.

If you play a class that can focus on their primary attack as the main damage source (like Demon Hunter), you can try to focus on buffs for your primary attack and 
 increasing your attack speed to get a higher DPS (Damage per second)
3. Critical Hit Chance & Critical Hit Damage
Another strategy would be to focus on increasing your Critical Hit Chance and Critical Hit Damage so you regularly deal 200-300% damage

Putting harmful effects on your enemies and killing them with damage over time is another strategy you can focus on.
 This requires really specific Essences, Set-Pieces, Legendary Gems and a focus on Potency.

Why do the damage yourself when your minions can do it for you? This is another way to improve your damage output. 
 Focus on summon damage through reforgig and magic affixes as well asShepherds Set Piece, Echoing Shade Legendary Gem and improving your primary attack, 
 as your summons will deal most of their damage with this.
How much damage you actually deal to an enemy in PVE is determined by the following formulas
Your Actual Damage is the Damage of your Skill (which you can see in your skills sheet) multiplied by different % modifiers of 5 categories
Damage Modifiers within a category are additive, not multiplicative. If for example a legendary gem increases your damage by 24% and another gem increases it by 16%,
this means your damage is increased by 40% (24+16), and not by 43,84% (1,24*1,16)
[Skill Damage] = SKILL_DMG x GENmod x LEGmod x EFFmod x COMmod x CRITmod
[Attack Damage] = ATK_DMG x GENmod x LEGmod x EFFmod x COMmod x CRITmod x ATKSpeed

All Sources of Armor Penetration can be found on the "Attributes" tab.
The Critical Hit Damage stat can be found on your character sheet and is improved by various sources (see "Attributes")
The effective damage is the average damage over an infinite number of hits. It factors in the damage you deal when landing Critical Hits.
The formula above just shows how much damage 1 attack can do. It does not factor in attack speed.
How much DPS (Damage per second) is done depends on the Number of Attacks (APS) and the damage per Attack.
DPS = APS x [1 + ATK_MODIFIERS] x ATK_DMG
APS is class specifc. For example without any buff the Attack Rate (for Demon Hunter) is 113,6 BPM or 1,89 Attacks per second (APS).
Attack Speed Bonus is capped at 100%, so the maximum Attacks per second would be 3,79.
Attack Speed modifiers come from different sources and either add permanent attack speed buffs or temporary buffs. It is capped at 100% max.
The Damage per Attack is the sum of the actual damage of both Primary Attack Damage and Skill Damage, if a skill is executed alongside the primary attack (like Vengeance).
This additional skill damages has to be factored in by the number of "executions" per Attack = R.
For example Vengeance shoots 2 additional arrows per attack, so R=2
Impale shoots an additional knife every 3 attacks, so R = 1/3.
ATK_DMG = SKILL_DMGPA x MODIFIERSPA + SKILL_DMG x MODIFIERS x R
The (actual) Damage that your primary attack does. As mentioned above it is calculated by SKILL_DMG x MODIFIERS
As mentioned above there are numerous ways to increase it.
Some Essences can modify skills to act as buffs that add additional SKILL_DMG to your primary attacks
Depending on how often per attack the SKLL_DMG is added, the damage here is modified by a factor R.
For example Vengeance launches 2 additional Shots per Attack (R = 2) while Impale only fires an additional knife every third attack (R = 1/3).
